steps.action: Opened the Google Cloud console (owner already signed in) and tried to create a project
steps.observation: Cloud showed 'access blocked' and required 2-step verification before any project could be created. The owner enabled it; after that the new-project form opened.

steps.action: Created a throwaway project named oauthpath-test-20261029 (no organization)
steps.observation: Created with no terms, billing or free-trial prompt. The console stayed on the owner's older project until switched by project ID.

steps.action: Opened Google Auth Platform > Get started and typed the app name
steps.observation: Four-part wizard: App information, Audience, Contact information, Finish. Support and contact emails must be real addresses, so the owner finished it; the agent did not see the last screen.
Audience is External, status Testing, cap of 100 users counted over the app's lifetime. Publish is disabled until Branding is complete. Adding test users needs a real email, so none were added.

steps.action: Opened Data Access > Add or remove scopes and declared gmail.readonly through the pasted-scopes box, then saved
steps.observation: The picker lists only scopes of enabled APIs, so Gmail scopes were absent. After pasting, the console filed gmail.readonly under 'restricted scopes'. The saved scope persisted after a reload.

steps.action: Opened Clients > Create OAuth client ID
steps.observation: The form opens with an Application type selector. No client was created, to avoid showing a secret.

steps.action: Cleanup: the owner shut down the test project; the agent confirmed the console's notice
steps.observation: The console said the project 'is shut down and scheduled to be deleted'. Google keeps it for a recovery period before deletion. No client or secret was ever created.

stoppedAt: the OAuth client creation step (guide step 4): no client or secret was created; steps 5 to 10 were not attempted

corrections.docClaim: A Google Cloud account and a Google Cloud project.
corrections.observed: A Google account with 2-step verification turned on was needed before Cloud would create a project: the console showed 'access blocked' until it was enabled.

corrections.docClaim: The sources do not say which individual Gmail scopes are classified as restricted. Check Google's OAuth API verification FAQ scope list for the exact scopes you plan to request.
corrections.observed: In the console, gmail.readonly was listed under 'restricted scopes' when declared on 2026-10-29. The scope picker only lists scopes of enabled APIs, so scopes may need to be pasted.
